Taraba Attack: 62 Killed and Thousands Displaced After Gunmen Raid Binnari Community

A deadly attack on Binnari community in Taraba State has left 62 people dead, dozens injured and thousands displaced, according to figures released by Nigeria's emergency management authorities.

By LokkeeVerse · 3 min read

Deadly Attack Leaves Binnari Community in Shock

A deadly attack on Binnari community in Taraba State has left residents facing a major humanitarian crisis after gunmen reportedly killed 62 people and forced thousands to flee their homes.

The attack occurred on October 23, 2026, in Binnari, located in Karim-Lamido Local Government Area of the state.

The National Emergency Management Agency confirmed the casualty figures in an update following an assessment by the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency.

According to the report, 62 people were killed, while another 52 sustained injuries.

The incident has raised fresh concerns about insecurity in parts of northeastern Nigeria.

Thousands Forced to Leave Their Homes

Beyond the reported deaths and injuries, the attack has created a serious displacement problem.

NEMA reported that approximately 5,187 residents were displaced following the incident.

The agency also estimated that 7,123 people were affected by the attack.

Many residents reportedly fled after gunmen invaded the community, leaving homes, businesses and other property damaged.

The displacement has created an urgent need for food, shelter, medical attention and other essential supplies.

What Happened During the Attack?

Reports indicate that the attackers invaded Binnari village shortly after Friday prayers.

The gunmen reportedly arrived in large numbers and opened fire, creating panic among residents.

Shops, homes, food supplies and motorcycles were also reportedly targeted during the attack.

The Taraba State Police Command initially confirmed that 10 bodies had been recovered from the scene.

However, subsequent reports from community sources and emergency management authorities indicated that the death toll had risen significantly.

The updated figure of 62 deaths was reported by NEMA following an assessment of the affected community.

NEMA Responds to the Humanitarian Situation

Following the attack, NEMA said its Yola Operations Office was working with the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency and other relevant authorities.

The agencies are expected to coordinate assistance for displaced residents and assess the needs of affected households.

The immediate humanitarian priorities include emergency shelter, food distribution, medical assistance and support for families who lost relatives.

The agency also expressed condolences to those who lost loved ones in the attack.

Security Concerns in Taraba State

The attack has renewed concerns about the security situation in rural communities across parts of Nigeria.

Remote settlements can be particularly vulnerable when security personnel are not readily available to respond to sudden attacks.

For residents, the consequences extend beyond the immediate loss of life.

Families may lose their homes, sources of income, food supplies and access to essential services.

The incident also places additional pressure on local authorities and humanitarian organisations working to support displaced communities.

What Happens Next?

The priority is to provide assistance to survivors and displaced families while strengthening security around affected communities.

Authorities will also need to investigate the attack and establish the identities of those responsible.

The scale of the reported casualties makes a coordinated response particularly important.

For Binnari residents, recovery will require more than immediate relief supplies. Families will need sustained support to rebuild their lives and regain access to safe housing and basic services.
